title: Bosonic Condensed Phase Real-time Dynamics from Ring Polymer Molecular Dynamics
authors: Yotam M. Y. Feldman, Sourav Karmakar, Sutirtha Paul, Jacob Higer, Adrian Del Maestro, Barak Hirshberg
abstract: We present a method for approximating real-time correlation functions and quantum transport coefficients of bosonic condensed phases. The direct evaluation of quantum real-time correlation functions in the path integral formulation is impossible due to a severe dynamical sign problem. Evaluating imaginary-time correlation functions and inverting them using analytic continuation is famously ill-posed. Ring polymer molecular dynamics (RPMD) provides an alternative approach resulting in accurate approximations for real-time correlation functions of condensed phases but neglects exchange effects. In this work, we develop a bosonic RPMD method, which is exact in the harmonic, short time, and high temperature limits. A critical enabling observation is that the Kubo-transformed correlation function for bosons is real only when the correlated observables are symmetric under exchange. We benchmark the method on harmonic and anharmonic model systems and then use it to directly obtain the Lieb-Liniger gas density-density real-time correlation functions at various temperatures and momentum transfers. This work enables the direct simulation of finite-temperature, real-time dynamics of large bosonic condensed phases using RPMD for the first time.
summary: The paper introduces an advanced bosonic Ring Polymer Molecular Dynamics (RPMD) method to calculate real-time correlation functions for interacting bosons. This technique bypasses the severe dynamical sign problem inherent in direct quantum simulations. It successfully enables the first direct simulation of finite-temperature, real-time dynamics for large bosonic condensed phases.
main_problem: The primary goal is developing a method to accurately approximate real-time correlation functions and quantum transport coefficients for bosonic condensed phases.
main_result: The authors developed a bosonic Ring Polymer Molecular Dynamics (RPMD) method that enables the direct simulation of finite-temperature, real-time dynamics for large bosonic systems using RPMD for the first time.
method: They extend standard RPMD by incorporating bosonic exchange symmetry into the classical ring polymer Hamiltonian and utilizing the Kubo-transformed correlation function estimator.
model_or_system: The work focuses on bosonic condensed phases, benchmarked on harmonic and anharmonic model systems, and applied specifically to the Lieb-Liniger gas (1D bosons with contact interactions).
key_observables: Real-time correlation functions (e.g., density-density), quantum transport coefficients, and the Dynamic Structure Factor (DSF).
important_parameters: Temperature ($ eta$), time ($t$), momentum transfer ($k/k_F$), and the number of ring polymer beads ($P$).
main_assumptions: The method is exact in the harmonic, short-time, and high-temperature limits; it relies on the assumption that correlated observables are symmetric under particle exchange for bosons.
figures_summary: Figures compare bosonic vs. distinguishable particle dynamics (e.g., position autocorrelation), showing how the bosonic symmetry manifests dynamically, and illustrate the accuracy of the method across different anharmonic potentials.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the general problem (sign problem in real-time quantum simulation) before developing the specific bosonic RPMD formalism. It then benchmarks this method on simple models (harmonic/anharmonic traps) to validate its theoretical limits and finally applies it to complex systems like the Lieb-Liniger gas.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, non-perturbative tool for simulating real-time quantum dynamics in bosonic many-body systems, overcoming major limitations associated with path integral methods.
